rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should establish a baseline. Testing a simple RNA-only model with PCA encoding (config_001) clarifies the baseline performance of the RNA modality without image data. This reduces uncertainty about the importance of multimodal fusion and provides a reference point for comparing more complex configurations later.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (RNA-only, singleprofile) achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests multiprofile with avgpool aggregation, isolating the effect of profile setting and aggregation method. It balances exploration by expanding from singleprofile to multiprofile while keeping RNA encoder and image encoder consistent, providing critical insights into whether multiprofile data or aggregation improves performance.

The existing evidence shows that multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002, 0.5907 accuracy) outperform singleprofile models. This experiment tests whether upgrading the RNA encoder from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200 (a more sophisticated latent space model) further improves accuracy while maintaining the effective multiprofile setting. It isolates the impact of RNA encoder quality, a critical design choice, without changing other factors like aggregation or fusion. This balances exploitation of the promising multiprofile direction with exploration of better encoders.

The existing evidence shows that using multiprofile and scvi_n200 RNA encoder (config_005) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.650124). This experiment tests adding image data (resnet50) with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion, building on the best RNA-only setup. It clarifies whether multimodal approaches can further improve performance, balancing exploration of image data with the proven RNA encoder.

The existing evidence shows that RNA-only models with scvi_n200 encoder and multiprofile setting (config_005) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.6501). This experiment tests whether adding image data (resnet50) to this strong RNA-only baseline can improve performance, isolating the effect of multimodal fusion. It balances exploration (testing multimodal) with exploitation (using proven RNA settings) and addresses a key design choice (image modality integration).

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l (config_036) achieve the highest accuracy (0.715). This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (vs concat in config_036) improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It balances exploitation (building on the top-performing model) and exploration (testing a key design choice).

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_036) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.715). This experiment tests replacing avgpool aggregation (used in config_036) with transformer aggregation, which could better capture complex interactions between modalities. This comparison isolates the impact of aggregation method on performance, a critical design choice with potential for significant gains. Testing transformer aggregation here directly addresses uncertainty about whether this method outperforms avgpool in multimodal settings.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_038: 0.7207). This experiment tests whether switching to scgpt RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion could further improve performance, isolating the effect of RNA representation and fusion strategy. It balances exploration of new encoders with exploitation of proven components (imagenet_vit_l and transformer).

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and concat fusion (config_038) achieve the highest validation accuracy of 0.7207. This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion instead of concat fusion improves performance, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. It is the best use of the final experiment as it directly compares two critical design choices (fusion methods) in the top-performing configuration.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l achieve high accuracy (e.g., config_039: 0.725). This experiment tests whether using scgpt (a more advanced RNA encoder) with concat fusion instead of weighted fusion could further improve performance, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder and fusion method. It is the best use of the final experiment to explore a promising but untested combination.
